heuristics.statement: Model premise, four clauses. Let F be a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values. For the fixed target, the probability that the single attempt of the search succeeds, with the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q (f(x) = the complete 7-round digest of the 128-byte message P || K || x, P the fixed first block, K the fixed prefix, q the fixed digest-plane mask of the generated circuit), is at least the probability P_F, over the fresh word r and a uniformly random F, that the same search succeeds when every evaluation of g is replaced by F (lazy sampling). Clauses: (a) distinct evaluated inputs collide with probability 2^-256, uniform and independent outputs; (b) the iterates from r + t have the first-collision law of a random mapping; (c) a point is a distinguished point (low 24 bits all ones and the next 98 bits below 2027) with probability 2027 / 2^122, independently of the collision events; (d) adaptivity: the program chooses its points, and which trails finish, are cut or abort, from earlier outputs of g; given the whole history of the run and which later outputs are distinguished points, a fresh evaluation equals a given earlier non-distinguished output with probability at least 2^-256 (the lazy-sampling hazard of F). Proof.md Section 4 (Lemma 2) proves P_F >= 0.39 for F from the hazard alone; (d) is the premise that g has that hazard. This is a comparison of two success events, not a statement about the entropy of r. Nothing else in the success bound is heuristic.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target blake3-r7-prefix-v1 restricted to 128-byte messages P || K || x, the fixed block P, prefix K and mask q, the 2^128-scale evaluation of g along about129541 trails including256 initial lanes started from r + t, 256 trails at a time. Not claimed for other messages, other round counts, or evaluations beyond this scale. The selected plan uses tmax131267 and explicit B1324689921494000000000000000000000000; checkpoint extension changes only representation and recovery work.
heuristics.extrapolation: Declared and not proved: an assumption, no proof is known. The full 256-bit functional graph, trails longer than 2^40 and 2^128 evaluations cannot be observed. The organizer experiments bsrho-n18 and proj-k0-w256 run this program on the real target at reduced width (the search at width 18) and at full width for 1024 points with 20-bit projections; they are program checks, reproducible observations consistent with the premise; no number of the claim is estimated from their counts. P and K were selected only by the gate count of the step (eight round-0 constants and the prefix price), not by any output of g. If the actual collision hazard is lower than assumed, the claimed success bound can fail and the time budget must be recalculated.
heuristics.limitations: A model premise about a fixed function, not a theorem. Reduced-width/projection experiments do not establish full-scale behavior. The certified margin above0.39 is about1.0004e-9. Any material hazard deficit requires a new budget.

heuristics.statement: Declared machine convention (supporting; the register-file convention of 7f3e749d-2c1e-4555-8c34-5e4ac9011927, a convention, not a claim about the benchmark). The cost model prices a 256-bit word RAM with loads and stores and fixes no register count or instruction set; this entry declares R = 776 registers of 256 bits, counted as 24832 bytes of memory and addressable by loads and stores, and charges every operation, load, store and register move; a conditional branch tests one register for zero, and a comparison is charged separately wherever a branch needs one. The main loop (one batch of 256 lanes, 44156 operations) has no load, store or move because the generated line needs 773 registers (output plane j in the register of input plane j). The organizer's reference count C(r7) = 1470 is used only as the unit. Code is memory and its format is not fixed by the cost model: a register-only gate is a 4-byte record, a packed-recovery instruction4bytes with7-bit operands and a separately charged constant-register pool, every other instruction 9 bytes (at most 64 with a 256-bit immediate at 37 bytes), and the images of the circuit generator and of the scan 36 bytes per wasm instruction. Passing-budget enforcement is charged two additional operations on every passing batch (a decrement and a zero-test branch, the pattern of the loop counter), with27 bytes of static code (the predecessor's three-instruction allowance, retained) and32 bytes for its counter. The opening proof gives the17-operation direct packed DP predicate, counted initialization,128-register recovery layout and source structural assertions.
heuristics.scope: The loop body of one batch of 256 lanes, its stage-1 test and the handlers; table walks, recovery, events, setup and the scan are charged at the stated bounds including loads and stores of their words.
heuristics.extrapolation: A machine with fewer than 776 registers would add loads and stores to every batch; a machine whose branches need a comparison would add 2 operations per batch; the claim assumes the declared convention.
heuristics.limitations: The benchmark profile does not fix a register count or an instruction set; the declaration is this entry's own (inherited from 7f3e749d-2c1e-4555-8c34-5e4ac9011927). The count 44142 is produced by the generator in the program (its C port emits the identical program in a memory-capped wasm sandbox, proof 3.6) and the register allocation by `allocate`.
